blocks.content:
India follows an integrated judicial system, unlike the dual system followed in some countries.
Structure of Courts in India:
• Supreme Court (Top level)
• High Courts (State level)
• Subordinate Courts (District and lower courts)

This system ensures uniform interpretation of laws across the country.
The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India follows an integrated judicial system with the Supreme Court at the top, High Courts at the state level, and Subordinate Courts at lower levels.
The integrated system ensures uniform interpretation of laws across the entire country.
The Supreme Court was established on 28 January 1950, replacing the Federal Court of India.
Located in New Delhi, the Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority and acts as the guardian of the Constitution under Article 124.
Article 124 specifically relates to the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court replaced the Federal Court of India on 28 January 1950.
Unlike dual judicial systems, India's integrated structure ensures uniform interpretation of laws.
